component: OpenStack Keystone (application credentials and EC2 credentials)
classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: The EC2 credential creation endpoint (UserOSEC2CredentialsResourceListCreate.post in keystone/api/users.py) did not call _check_unrestricted_application_credential, which the application-credential create and delete endpoints in the same file already call, so a token from a restricted application credential with only the reader role could mint an EC2/S3 credential carrying all of the parent user's S3 permissions.
notes: OSSA-2026-005. Affects Keystone >= 14.0.0; fixed in 26.1.1, 27.0.1, 28.0.1 and 29.0.1. Stable backports per the Launchpad bug: 5d5ae3aea3b90fd7fa4eaf3d3b918418db138b2e (2026.1), 24b0e1190b04701614659a74d5a5b644902a77b8 (2025.2), 4da764003370b2d8b61a214aecf6183e7b53ecd7 (2025.1). Only deployments that combine restricted application credentials with the EC2/S3 API are affected. The fix also tightens the ec2 create and delete policies to require the member role. A later Keystone issue about the project scope of EC2 credentials (OSSA-2026-015, CVE-2026-43001) has a different root cause and is not this sample. That the application-credential endpoints call the guard was read on the current master branch of keystone/api/users.py; the fix commit message says it adds the existing guard to the EC2 endpoint.

root_cause: The agent's edit_file tool could only write inside the project, and there EditFileTool::needs_confirmation always returned false, so model output could create or change the project-local .zed/settings.json, whose always_allow_tool_actions then switched off confirmation for every later tool call, including the terminal; 0.197.3 asks for confirmation for any path with a .zed component, under the global config directory, or outside the project.
notes: Affected < 0.197.3; v0.197.3 is the first stable release of the 0.197 line. needs_confirmation was read at v0.197.1-pre (always false) and at v0.197.3 (checks for a .zed component, the global config dir and paths outside the project). The advisory names no commit; PRs #35221 and #35224 (merged 2025-07-28) introduce the new checks per the file history and release notes, so they are listed as the fix. OSV lists dd60cc285b759e23c9de0eaee9513dc707d212d2, an unrelated User-Agent cherry-pick, which is not used. v0.197.2-pre was not checked. The advisory says edits to the global settings file were already blocked; only the project-local settings layer was open.

component: Fluid (CSI node plugin RBAC in the Helm chart)
root_cause: The Helm chart gave the fluid-csi service account, whose token sits on every node through the CSI node-plugin DaemonSet, cluster-wide get and patch on nodes and every verb on nodes/proxy, although the plugin only needs to act on its own node, so control of one node let an attacker change every node's spec; 0.8.6 removes these rules and uses the kubelet's node-bound credentials.
symbols: nodes and nodes/proxy rules of the CSI plugin's ClusterRole
notes: Affects 0.7.0 through 0.8.5; fixed in 0.8.6. The fix commit merges the GHSA fork; ^ means its first parent (1cc14b3 per the commit page, short hash only). The fix adds a --kubelet-kube-config flag and mounts the kubelet kubeconfig and certificates so the plugin acts with node-bound credentials, and narrows the events rules. Render the chart before auditing. Workaround in the advisory: delete the csi-nodeplugin-fluid DaemonSet or use sidecar mode.

component: Azure Storage account shared for open-source model downloads (Microsoft AI research)
root_cause: To let the public download models, a researcher published in a public GitHub README an Account SAS token that granted full control (read, write, delete) over the whole storage account instead of read access to one container, with its expiry extended to 2051, so the link exposed about 38 TB of internal data (workstation backups, Teams messages) and allowed files to be overwritten.
audit_scope: The shared access signature published for the robust-models-transfer model downloads and the storage account it granted access to (question-level only; the token was revoked on 2023-06-24)
notes: No CVE. Mode A only. Reported by Wiz on 2023-06-22, mitigated on 2023-06-24, MSRC blog on 2023-09-18. The MSRC post only says 'overly-permissive'; the account-wide full-control scope, the Account SAS type and the 2051 expiry come from Wiz. Wiz names the repository robust-models-transfer; github.com/microsoft/robust-models-transfer returned 404 on 2026-09-25, so no repository URL is given. Microsoft's follow-up was to extend GitHub secret scanning to SAS tokens with overly permissive expiry or privileges.

component: Flashbots mev-boost-relay getPayload (run by the Ultra Sound relay)
root_cause: handleGetPayload in services/api/service.go returned the full execution payload to the proposer after checking only the signature on the blinded header, and published the block asynchronously (and not at all behind a feature flag), so a proposer could sign a header for a block the network would reject, see the builder's transactions, and then propose its own block that reordered them; PR #330 publishes the block first and withholds the payload when publishing fails.
notes: Off-chain relay code, so onchain is null. Parent of the fix commit is 75d9525dbd63c59c11e52a6d8efcf0b3d68bec8c. The fix removed the ffDisableBlockPublishing flag, made publishing synchronous before the response, and added GETPAYLOAD_DELAY_MS; released as v1.0.0-alpha3 and deployed on 2023-04-03 per the post-mortem. The related late-request timing issue has its own fix (commit d995711da8b887bf5e892858086ecfa37d2db4cc) and is not this root cause. Loss of about $20M to sandwich bots per the post-mortem.

root_cause: With more than one Pedersen commitment, gnark checked all the commitments' proofs of knowledge in one batched pairing equation that used the same sigma for every commitment, so only the combination was bound; a prover could move committed content between commitments and fix all but one of them (for example to a constant) before choosing the witness, which made the in-circuit challenges hashed from those commitments known in advance; v0.11.0 uses a separate sigma per commitment.
notes: Only circuits with more than one commitment are affected; the advisory's workaround is a single commitment plus std/multicommit. The fix commit hash is from the advisory and OSV; the commit page returned 404 through the fetch tool, so functions are not listed. Paths are from Zellic's write-up and name only the bn254 backend; other curves were not checked. Commitment key generation and the batched proof-of-knowledge check also involve the pedersen package of gnark-crypto, a separate repository. The zero-knowledge issue reported with it (GHSA-9xcg-3q8v-7fq6) has a different root cause.

root_cause: find_server() in src/objects.c applied the client's tracked startup parameters (varcache_apply) to the server connection even when that connection was about to run auth_query as auth_user for a client that had not authenticated yet, so with search_path in track_extra_parameters an unauthenticated client chose the schema search path of the privileged authentication query, whose default text uses an unqualified operator; the fix skips varcache_apply when sending the auth query.
notes: Needs three settings together: search_path in track_extra_parameters (non-default), a non-empty auth_user (non-default), and an auth_query with unqualified names (the default auth_query uses an unqualified operator). Fixed in 1.25.1 per the project's changelog and news; the GHSA text says 1.25.0. Parent of the fix is f2c047596b36df51d584525d965c6c54a888ddc4. The fix commit also adds test_auth_query_no_set_commands in test/test_auth.py, and the release updated the documented auth_query example to set a safe search_path.

root_cause: When the Lua engine was set up (scriptingInit in src/eval.c, luaEngineInitEngine in src/function_lua.c), Redis protected the globals table but not the metatables of basic types such as strings, and still exposed getfenv, setfenv and newproxy, so a script from one ACL user could plant metamethods in the Lua state shared by all users that later ran inside another user's script with that user's permissions; the fix makes basic-type metatables read-only and puts the deprecated functions behind lua-enable-deprecated-api.
audit_scope: the Lua scripting sources in src (eval.c, function_lua.c, script_lua.c) with deps/lua for reference
notes: Fixed in 8.2.2, 8.0.4, 7.4.6, 7.2.11 and 6.2.20 per OSV. Parent of the fix is d5728cb5795c966c5b5b1e0f0ac576a7e69af539. The fix adds luaSetTableProtectionForBasicTypes and a hidden, immutable config lua-enable-deprecated-api. Workaround: block the EVAL and FUNCTION command families with ACL. Not related to RediShell (CVE-2025-49844, a use-after-free already in held-out-2).

component: needrestart (Python interpreter scan, runs as root)
classes: Which candidate a name resolves to
root_cause: To list a scanned Python process's modules, NeedRestart::Interp::Python::files copied PYTHONPATH from that process's /proc/<pid>/environ into its own environment and then started a Python interpreter as root, so the first place the interpreter searched for modules was a directory chosen by the unprivileged owner of the scanned process; the fix stops setting PYTHONPATH and reads the paths only as data, prefixed with /proc/<pid>/root.
notes: Fixed in needrestart 3.8. Parent of the fix is 6ce6136cccc307c6b8a0f8cae12f9a22ac2aad59. Qualys reported a sibling with the same pattern in the Ruby scanner (CVE-2024-48992, RUBYLIB) and a separate race on /proc/<pid>/exe (CVE-2024-48991); neither is this sample. needrestart runs as root from the package manager hook on Debian and Ubuntu.

classes: Which candidate a name resolves to
root_cause: JupyterApp.config_file_paths in jupyter_core/application.py put os.getcwd() at the front of the configuration search path, so a jupyter_*_config.py file (Python code) in whatever directory a user started a Jupyter command from was loaded first, letting another user who can write to a shared directory run code as that user; 4.11.2 removes the working directory from the search path.
notes: Affects jupyter_core <= 4.11.1; fixed in 4.11.2. The fix commit merges the GHSA fork; ^ means its first parent (d3f61f3 per the commit page, short hash only). The fix also adds test_load_config_no_cwd in jupyter_core/tests/test_application.py.

classes: Values that must not be guessable
root_cause: FormData.prototype._generateBoundary in lib/form_data.js built the multipart boundary from 24 Math.random() digits, and that boundary is the only thing that keeps attacker-controlled field values from being read as new parts; because Math.random state can be recovered from other outputs of the same process, the boundary could be predicted and extra parameters injected; 2.5.4, 3.0.4 and 4.0.4 use crypto.randomBytes.
notes: Affects < 2.5.4, 3.0.0-3.0.3 and 4.0.0-4.0.3. The listed commit is the one the advisories reference (parent d8d67dc, short hash only); which release line it is on was not confirmed, and the backports for the other lines are not listed. Exploiting it needs other Math.random outputs from the same process and control of one field. The fix adds test/integration/test-boundary-prediction.js.

component: uClibc-ng and uClibc DNS stub resolver
classes: Values that must not be guessable
root_cause: __dns_lookup in libc/inet/resolv.c took each query's DNS transaction ID from a static counter (last_id) that went up by one per query and reset to 2, and did not randomize the source port itself, so an off-path attacker could predict the ID of the next query and forge a matching answer; uClibc-ng 1.0.41 adds configurable random ID generation.
notes: uClibc-ng through 1.0.40 and uClibc through 0.9.33.2 are affected; the fix is in uClibc-ng 1.0.41. Parent of the fix is 592574ae535c35de500f6c3e8d8400d0bb0d985a. A follow-up commit, 2880524 ('DnsLookup: stdint, timeforced reseeding', 2022-05-29, short hash only), changes the same code. OSV's fixed commit 9e504a4ac839ac771ee96ea626d225adaa7df054 only bumps the version to 1.0.40 and is not used. Per the fix commit message, the default mode (PRNGPLUS) uses the libc PRNG reseeded from urandom or the clock, not a cryptographic source for every ID. The GitHub repository is a mirror of the project's own git server. No fix for the original uClibc was checked.
